earlier_scan.source_named: Vanhoudt, Bettie. 1987. Elements de description du leke, langue bantoue de zone C (MRAC 125; PHOIBLE files it under zmx); ToC online shows tone chapters only, suprasegmental pages not scanned

sources.citation: Vanhoudt, Bettie. 1987. Éléments de description du leke, langue bantoue de zone C. Tervuren: Musée royal de l'Afrique centrale, Annales Sciences humaines 125. 238 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number Loeb Music Library.15.10.7.1.1.6 (125)); ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan (also digitized at HathiTrust, search-only (in copyright))
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number MUS.15.10.7.1.1.6 (125)
sources.note: Only the Rosetta Project excerpts are open (ToC pp. I-VI; pp. 5-6, 15, 19, 152, 207, 221-223, 237-238). The ToC (p. II) shows the suprasegmental chapter as 'II. PHONEMES SUPRASEGMENTAUX 32: 1. Tonalité 32 (1.1 Tonèmes, 1.2 Limitations, 1.3 Réalisations phonétiques, 1.4 Exemples) 2. Quantité 36' and '2.2 Morphonologie supra-segmentale 104' — no accent/stress heading anywhere. The opened pages contain no statement about stress; the Introduction (p. 6) says the informant whistled the tonality of utterances. Pages 32-36 themselves are not scanned anywhere open.

sources.citation: Leitch, Myles Francis. 2009. Language and dialect in Epena district south. Annales Æquatoria 30: 787-838.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Dialectology of Dibole (EDS) vs Bomitaba (EDN); no prosodic description. Says the survey transcriptions 'did not mark tone'. p. 794: 'Bettie Van Houdt's (1987) Elements de Description du Leke is a notable exception (Leke is the variety of Bomitaba spoken in Mokengui). Van Houdt 1987 identified 4 dialectal variants of Bomitaba' — the only substantive linguistic study of Bomitaba it knows.

sources.citation: Gardner, William L. 1990 [published 2006]. Language use in the Epena district of Northern Congo. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2006-005 (MA thesis, University of North Dakota). 108 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 9: 'Therefore, neither my colleagues nor I recorded stress or tone on the wordlists.. A more thorough phonological study, including tone and stress, should be conducted in the future'. Key to symbols (p. 26) lists high/low tone marks only. No statement on stress placement.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 28 segments plus high-tone and low-tone marks; nothing on stress.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology; dialects Northern (Matoki) and Central (Epena).

sources.citation: Leitch, Myles Francis. 1997. Vowel harmonies of the Congo Basin: an Optimality Theory analysis of variation in the Bantu zone C. PhD dissertation, University of British Columbia.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Zone-C comparative phonology by the linguist who worked in Epena district; may cite Leke/Bomitaba data from Vanhoudt with remarks on prosody (tone, absence of stress) for the group.

sources.citation: Ndinga Oba, Antoine. 1995. Esquisse phonologique du Bomitaba: langue bantu de la zone C (Congo). Brazzaville: Université Marien Ngouabi. 28 pp.

sources.note: A dedicated phonological sketch of Bomitaba proper (not just the Leke idiolect); a Congolese phonologist's esquisse would normally have a short suprasegmental section.
